data.body:
Root cause CONFIRMED and reproduced deterministically.

The shared-base assertion at _assert_emit_is_append_only is a fixture precondition, and clone
B's sync to it was an unasserted side effect of _engine_run(repo_b, 'list'). That read path
(rebar._engine_support.reads.ensure_fresh) is best-effort BY DESIGN: /tmp marker throttle,
reconverge under a deliberately short lock timeout, and every failure swallowed ('a read must
never fail because a fetch could not run'). The read returns 0 whether or not the pull landed,
so under CI load B keeps a stale base and the test fails while building its own setup.

Reproduction: forcing the incidental sync to be a no-op with REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off (which
ensure_fresh honours) fails ALL THREE two-clone-union tests on unmodified main with exactly
the reported signature, AssertionError: clones do not share a base. Leaving sync enabled,
they pass. That isolates the flake to the best-effort side effect and rules out a defect in
sidecar emit.

Fix pushed as Gerrit change 1652: new _sync_from_origin(tracker) helper does a checked
git fetch + git merge --ff-only so a failed sync raises at the setup step that owns it, and
both preconditions are now labelled SETUP (not the I1 invariant) with set-difference detail.
Deterministic sync, no retry loop, no timing assertions.

Verified locally: the 3 tests pass under REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off (AC3), all 29 tests in the file
pass under the default env (AC4), make lint and make typecheck clean (AC5).
